(Columbus, Ohio) | college = [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2012–2016) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] ([[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2014]]) * [[Associated Press]] All-Ohio Second Team (2012) * ''[[Columbus Dispatch]]'' Metro Co-Player of the Year (2012) * [[Ohio High School Athletic Association|OHSAA]] Division I state champion (2012) }} '''Caris Coleman LeVert''' (born August 25, 1994) is an American basketball player who completed his [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] career during his senior season for the [[2015–16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2015–16 team]]. His senior season was ended early due to injury. As a freshman for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 team]], he nearly [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] but earned a key role off the bench as the team went on to reach the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship game]] in the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. As a sophomore for the [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14 team]], he became a regular starter and was selected as a second team [[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2013–14 All-Big Ten]] player for the outright Big Ten regular season champions. During his first two years at Michigan, he was notable as the training partner of back-to-back [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Players of the Year]] [[Trey Burke]] (also [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]]) and [[Nik Stauskas]]. He was a 2012 [[Associated Press]] All-Ohio Second Team high school basketball player and the 2012 ''[[Columbus Dispatch]]'' Metro Player of the Year for the 2012 [[Ohio High School Athletic Association]] (OHSAA) Division I state champion [[Pickerington High School Central]] in Ohio. He was a 2014–15, and 2015–16 preseason All-Big Ten first team selection and a preseason All-American according to many selectors, but he suffered an injury midway through his junior season for the [[2014–15 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2014–15 team]]. LeVert is related to [[Eddie Levert]], [[Gerald Levert]] and [[Sean Levert]]. ==Early life== LeVert grew up in Northeast [[Columbus, Ohio|Columbus]] but moved to nearby [[Pickerington, Ohio|Pickerington]] in second grade. As a high school senior, he led Pickerington High School Central to a 26–2 record and the 2012 OHSAA Division I state championship. LeVert was a 2012 [[Associated Press]] All-Ohio Second Team high school basketball player and the 2012 ''[[Columbus Dispatch]]'' Metro Player of the Year for [[Pickerington High School Central]]. He was not heavily recruited in high school and his only official visit was to [[Alabama State Hornets basketball|Alabama State]].{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2014/10/16/michigan-wolverines-caris-levert-nik-stauskas-trey-burke-guard/17387247/|title=Caris LeVert aims to be next Michigan guard to step up|accessdate=2014-10-21|date=2014-10-16|author=Snyder, Mark|work=[[USA Today]]}} He committed to play basketball for [[John Groce]] and the [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball]] program in November 2011. Meanwhile, when future teammates [[Mitch McGary]] and Stauskas joined [[Glenn Robinson III]] by committing to Michigan in November 2011, Michigan became the fifth best recruiting class in the country.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/story/_/id/7186833/no-2-ranked-prep-prospect-mitch-mcgary-commits-michigan|title=Mitch McGary commits to Michigan|accessdate=2011-11-18|date=2011-11-03|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Jordan, Jason}}{{cite web|url=http://annarbor.com/sports/um-basketball/with-mitch-mcgary-in-tow-michigan-basketball-now-has-a-top-five-class-for-2012/|title=With Mitch McGary in tow, Michigan basketball now has a top five class for 2012|accessdate=2011-11-18|date=2011-11-03|work=[[AnnArbor.com]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}} When Groce got hired by [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball]] in March 2012, LeVert got lost in the shuffle and decided to commit to Michigan.{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/03/caris-levert-would-be-at-illinois-if-john-groce-had-picked-up-the-phone/|title=Caris LeVert would be at Illinois if John Groce had picked up the phone|accessdate=2014-03-13|date=2014-03-03|author=Dauster, Rob|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]}} Ironically, Groce's [[2011–12 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|2011–12 Ohio Bobcats]]' upset of the [[2011–12 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2011–12 Michigan team]] in the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] was probably the reason that Groce was hired by Illinois and LeVert withdrew his [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for Ohio.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/caris-levert-development-michigan-verge-big-ten-title-201211409--ncaab.html|title=Caris LeVert's development has Michigan on the verge of a Big Ten title|accessdate=2014-03-13|date=2014-02-23|author=Eisenberg, Jeff|publisher=[[Yahoo! As a freshman, he began the year behind Stauskas, Robinson, [[Tim Hardaway, Jr.]], and Matt Vogrich on the [[depth chart]] for the [[shooting guard]]/[[small forward]] positions and did not play in the first six games as a result. LeVert was a part of an incoming class that included McGary, Stauskas, Robinson, and [[Spike Albrecht]].{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/02/28/assigned-reading-caris-leverts-defining-moment/|title=Assigned Reading: Caris LeVert's defining moment|accessdate=2014-03-14|date=2014-02-28|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|author=Payne, Terrence}} Eventually, Michigan [[head coach]] [[John Beilein]] decided that LeVert had value as a perimeter defender and decided to play him rather than redshirt him.{{cite web|url=http://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2014/01/07/rising-star-michigan-guard-caris-levert/|title=Rising Star: Michigan Guard Caris LeVert|accessdate=2014-03-13|date=2014-01-07|publisher=[[KYW-TV]]|author=Kahn, Andrew}} On December 1 against [[2012–13 Bradley Braves men's basketball team|Bradley]] Beilein juggled his lineup: Stauskas made his first career regular season start and LeVert saw his first action.{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=323360071|title=(3) Michigan 74 (7-0, 1-0 away); Bradley 66 (5-2, 3-1 home)|accessdate=2012-12-01|date=2012-12-01|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/120112aac.html|title=Postgame Notes: #3 Michigan 74, Bradley 66|accessdate=2012-12-02|date=2012-12-01|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}} By late December, LeVert became the one-on-one partner for Burke after practices.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2012/12/michigans_columbus_connection.html|title=Michigan's Columbus connection: Trey Burke taking frosh Caris LeVert under his wing this season|accessdate=2014-03-15|date=2012-12-22|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}} LeVert made his first start on December 29 against [[2012–13 Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball team|Central Michigan]], when [[Tim Hardaway, Jr.]] was unavailable. The 3 freshmen in the starting lineup—Robinson, Stauskas and LeVert—combined for 48 points, 12 rebounds and 8 assists.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=323640130|title=Trey Burke leads No. 2 Michigan past Central Michigan|accessdate=2015-03-15|date=2012-12-29|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/122912aad.html|title=Postgame Notes: #2 Michigan 88, Central Michigan 73|accessdate=2015-03-15|date=2012-12-29|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}} That night LeVert tallied 9 points and 5 assists.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=323640130|title=Cent Michigan 73 (7-6, 1-3 away); (2) Michigan 88 (13-0, 9-0 home)|accessdate=2015-03-15|date=2012-12-29|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} LeVert averaged 2.3 [[point (basketball)|points]] in under 11 minutes of play per game. He never scored in double digits as a freshman, but he scored 8 points each in [[2012–13 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|conference]] wins over [[2012–13 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] and [[2012–13 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] as well as the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] final four victory over [[2012–13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] in 21 minutes of play. ===2013–14 season=== [[File:20140102 Caris LeVert (1).JPG|thumb|LeVert in the [[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2013–14 Big Ten season]] opener at [[Williams Arena]] against [[2013–14 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]]]] LeVert's classmates all made names for themselves as freshmen.
